summary: This is the domain class for the weather app: a small, read-only record of one day's weather, holding the date, the temperature in Celsius, and the condition. The stream pipelines in the app filter, map, and average collections of these objects.

lines.code: private final double celsius;   // temperature in °C
lines.text: The temperature is stored once, in Celsius, and marked final so it can never change after construction. Keeping a single source of truth means the Fahrenheit conversion later becomes a map step over the stream rather than a second field to keep in sync.

lines.code: private final String condition; // e.g., Sunny, Rainy, Cloudy
lines.text: The condition is a plain String, so the filter that finds rainy days will compare text. Be consistent about spelling and capitalization when you create entries, because "Rainy" and "rainy" are different values to a String comparison.

lines.text: Because every field is final, the constructor is the only chance to set them; each entry arrives fully formed and stays that way. Immutable objects like this are exactly what streams like to work with.
The stream pipelines reach the data through getters like this one, which is what lets a lambda such as w -> w.getCelsius() feed a mapToDouble for the weekly average.
Overriding toString gives each entry a readable form, so printing a filtered stream of rainy days shows the date, temperature, and condition instead of a meaningless object hash.
